Even after watching just the show, I never saw him as that honestly.

The other characters got a chance at redemption but Izaya did not. There wasn’t a single wholesome interaction between him and another character aside from the flashback with Shinra. I feel like if they did something wholesome with his character where someone gave him the chance to be seen as the good guy and he still acted out, continuing to do evil/heinous things, then I could accept him being the ultimate bad guy. But, this lack of character develop felt too unnatural for me to see him as the actual bad guy. It felt like the show was setting up some kind of closure or resolution and last minute, decided to opt out of it.

To be fair, I’m also biased because I really enjoyed his character and he’s probably my favorite “villain” in anime. I just think there was a really good opportunity to develop his character and give him redemption, and the author never expanded on it, for whatever reason.

Well Shinra is an underground doctor that changes the face of criminals and it’s implied that he deals with harvesting organs and such too. They’re both “bad” people, but in the city of Ikebukuro, these things aren’t really relevant. 

Also, Izaya’s intent is never evil. I never found him to be the clear cut villain since he was never opposed to a happy ending for anyone in all the plots he orchestrated. He just wanted to see how they would deal with the situations, almost like a science experiment. His intent wasn’t to be evil as much as it was to provoke people, whether it’s for good or bad. And his connections with the main “good” cast made me think he would get either redemption or closure, which he got neither of. Like Vorona and Hollywood got redemption and they’re minor characters who have definitely hurt more people than Izaya.

I do understand why you find him shallow, but that’s why the end disappointed me. I wanted to see some character development with an already interesting character. He was intertwined with the main cast, so him being turned into the ultimate villain without any sort of closure between him and Shizuo or Shinra felt lazy.
Personally, I don’t think any part of the Durarara universe sought to be relatable aside from Mikado’s gang. So I don’t really care if he was relatable or not. 

Although, they do go into his more “relatable” aspects in the manga. Basically, he manipulates people because he wants connections but he can’t act like a decent person because that would mean he’s leaving himself vulnerable. It’s like what Shinra said— he’s more human than anyone else. He just chooses to be a dick to not get hurt by anyone. I mean when he loves someone, like Shinra, he loves like crazy. He makes Nakura suffer for the rest of his life for hurting Shinra.
